transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-25
Time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: 50 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood CSM), Jared Kim (Quantaco ML Eng), Anya Petrov (Quantaco Eng Mgr), Liam O'Neill (Quantaco CTO)

--- Auto-summary (brief) ---
Focus: cost/unit economics, tokens per second per dollar, caching savings observed in POC, batching tradeoffs, plan to finalize pilot metrics and next steps for procurement.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Samantha): okay hey everyone thanks for joining, quick check  can you see my screen?
00:12 Speaker 2 (Jared): yep seeing it, looks good, thanks.
00:18 Speaker 1 (Samantha): cool, so agenda: quick recap of last week's runs, dive into the tokens/sec per dollar numbers, caching numbers, and then batching tradeoffs. diego will run through the bench results.
00:32 Speaker 3 (Diego): alright, i'll share the key slides  um our staging runs used your 1k prompt set plus a longer tail of 2k conversational prompts, approx 3x concurrency shapes.
00:47 Speaker 3 (Diego): baseline hosted single-request mode, no batching, no cache: we observed about 350 tokens/sec per GPU at median, and cost unlocked was X  sorry, in cost units that translated to ~0.9M tokens per dollar per hour equivalent, crude but useful.
01:05 Speaker 4 (Anya): can you say that again  0.9M tokens per dollar? that feels off vs our internal numbers.
01:12 Speaker 3 (Diego): yeah so it's approximate  depends on sequence lengths. for your mix (avg seq 120 tokens) we saw roughly 900k tokens per $1 normalized to our hosted sku. there is noise in the tail.
01:30 Speaker 5 (Liam): what's the baseline latency? median vs p95?
01:36 Speaker 3 (Diego): median was ~70ms per token generating step? sorry per step, token latency looked good, but p95 tail grew when we used larger batch sizes. median end-to-end generation for prompts was about 220ms, p95 780ms on that config.
01:56 Speaker 2 (Jared): okay that aligns roughly. what about the kv cache numbers you mentioned last week?
02:02 Speaker 3 (Diego): great question  with prefix/KV cache enabled and a small warm-up set, we measured billable token reductions in the 18-22% band across the prompt set. important caveat: caching benefit skewed heavily toward repeated prefix patterns  your templates saw 24% reduction but free-form user text only 8-10%.
02:32 Speaker 4 (Anya): so 18-22% is aggregated  good. how does that translate to dollars  like tokens/sec/$ post-cache?
02:41 Speaker 3 (Diego): after cache, tokens per $ improved correspondingly  so where we had 900k tokens per $1 baseline, effective went up to roughly 1.08M tokens per $1 for the mixed mix (again, approximate). the cost per completed request dropped by ~12% in our model because of reduced generation tokens plus less re-run overhead.
03:05 Speaker 1 (Samantha): we also ran batching experiments  diego, can you summarize batching tradeoffs?
03:11 Speaker 3 (Diego): sure. small batches (2-4) increased GPU utilization modestly with negligible p95 impact; medium (8-16) gave ~2.1-2.8x throughput gains in tokens/sec but p95 latency worsened by roughly 1.5-2x depending on request mix; large batches (32+) delivered up to 3x throughput but pushed p95 above our SLO target for interactive app. so tradeoff: you get cost savings per token but worse tail latency.
03:46 Speaker 5 (Liam): do we have numbers for tokens/sec per dollar at batch=16 vs batch=1?
03:51 Speaker 3 (Diego): yes  for batch=16 we observed tokens/sec roughly 3.0x baseline, which maps to approx 2.6-2.8M tokens per $1 if cache also used. but end-to-end p95 in some runs hit ~1.4s which you said is too high for your use case.
04:12 Speaker 4 (Anya): right our SLAs are 500ms p95 for customer-facing real-time features. batch=16 sounds risky.
04:20 Speaker 2 (Jared): any middle ground? dynamic batching or adaptive qos?
04:25 Speaker 3 (Diego): yes we demoed dynamic batching in the runtime  it can batch opportunistically but prioritize low-latency requests, and we can set per-route batch caps. that gets you ~1.6-1.9x throughput improvement with p95 still within ~350-500ms depending on route.
04:45 Speaker 1 (Samantha): also worth noting dedicated capacity pricing looks favorable once you cross a utilization threshold  for your expected sustained throughput derived from your usage projections (you shared a 10k daily active requests estimate), dedicated committed pools reduce per-token cost by ~25-35% depending on commit level.
05:05 Speaker 5 (Liam): what's the delta in absolute dollars? do you have a sample scenario?
05:10 Speaker 3 (Diego): we modeled three scenarios in the spreadsheet  quick numbers: hosted paid-as-you-go case was roughly $0.00012 per 1k tokens (normalized), dedicated with monthly commit at 70% utilization dropped to around $0.00008 per 1k tokens effectively. these are illustrative and depend on your commit / autoscale behavior.
05:33 Speaker 4 (Anya): we'd need the spreadsheet. also can you show how batching + cache interacts  do we double-count savings?
05:40 Speaker 3 (Diego): good point  batching reduces GPU cost per token by raising throughput; cache reduces billable tokens. the effects are mostly multiplicative in our simple model: effective tokens/$ = baseline tokens/$ * batching_factor * (1/(1 - cache_reduction_fraction)). so if batching gives 3x and cache gives 20% reduction, then tokens/$ ~ 3x * 1.25 = 3.75x baseline roughly. but watch out for latency impact and warm-up hit.
06:15 Speaker 2 (Jared): understood  in practice warm-up for cache means first N requests won't benefit; we have to measure cold-start patterns.
06:22 Speaker 3 (Diego): exactly; we recommended a small warm-up ramp and an LRU TTL strategy for prefixes to keep high hit rates for common templates.
06:32 Speaker 1 (Samantha): quick aside on instrumentation  priya, did we push the token-level cost breakdown to their console?
06:37 Speaker 4 (Priya): yes we added token-level cost and p95 per-route in the dashboard; i pushed a link to the sheet in slack earlier, but i'll re-share after the call.
06:47 Speaker 5 (Liam): great. another question  security/procurement folks will want to see audit logs, KMS, SOC2. are we ready to present that?
06:55 Speaker 1 (Samantha): yes we have SOC 2 and audit logs, and private deployment options for on-prem and VPC. i'll attach the security pack in the follow-up.
07:05 Speaker 5 (Liam): thanks.
07:09 Speaker 2 (Jared): back to the numbers  what timeframe to get a final cost estimate we can share with finance?
07:15 Speaker 1 (Samantha): if we run the two additional bench tasks (diego's batch-cap comparison + cache hit rate sim) and you share last week's production-like prompt set, we can update the cost model by Friday 6/27.
07:26 Speaker 4 (Anya): ok i'll get those prompts out today.
07:29 Speaker 3 (Diego): quick note  we saw one outlier where a long token sequence spiked cost by 4x on a single request due to long context; suggested mitigation is to clip context or use condensed embeddings for long histories  saved about 30-40% on that path.
07:48 Speaker 2 (Jared): good to know. we'd prefer not to change customer UX, so maybe condensed embeddings approach.
07:54 Speaker 1 (Samantha): noted.
08:00 Speaker 5 (Liam): any thoughts on dedicated vs hosted from reliability perspective? i.e., if we go dedicated and have a failover region, what's the SLA?
08:10 Speaker 3 (Diego): dedicated pools come with SLA-backed uptime and region failover options; we can also set autoscale and burst capacity to the hosted plane if you want hybrid  routing policy can fallback to hosted compatible model variants but with higher cost.
08:26 Speaker 4 (Anya): so we can keep critical paths on dedicated and overflow non-critical on hosted?
08:31 Speaker 3 (Diego): yes that's a common pattern.
08:34 Speaker 1 (Samantha): are we ready to talk about procurement timeline?
08:37 Speaker 5 (Liam): finance will want 3 vendor options and our pilot metrics. can we get a one-pager with numbers?
08:44 Speaker 1 (Samantha): we'll produce a one-pager and the cost spreadsheet.
08:47 Speaker 2 (Jared): quick nit  some transcriptions in the dashboard show model name as redwood-latino instead of redwood-latency, minor but amusing.
08:58 Speaker 3 (Diego): (laughs) transcription got it wrong, yeah.
09:02 Speaker 4 (Anya): question: do you support per-token billing visibility broken down by model variant and quantization settings?
09:10 Speaker 3 (Diego): yes  per-route/model dashboards show per-token and per-request cost, breakdown by quantization profile and kernel selection. we can export the CSV for finance.
09:21 Speaker 5 (Liam): okay great.
09:25 Speaker 1 (Samantha): let's capture the action items  diego will run the batch vs dynamic batching benchmarks and cache on/off by 6/30; jared will share the 2k prompt set by EOD today; i'll send updated cost scenarios and security pack by 6/27. priya will re-share dashboard links.
09:45 Speaker 2 (Jared): got it.
09:48 Speaker 4 (Anya): anything else on the tech side?
09:52 Speaker 3 (Diego): we also noticed a small mem pressure on the GPU when running huge kv caches  for large prefix caches we recommend sizing memory appropriately or using external cache tier  flagging for infra.
10:08 Speaker 5 (Liam): noted.
10:11 Speaker 1 (Samantha): thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and a proposed 1-hour latency deep dive week of July 7th.
10:20 Speaker 2 (Jared): thanks all.
10:22 Speaker 1 (Samantha): bye.

--- End transcript ---
